simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to חָלָק (H2509) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: a.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: חָלָק (châlâq) means smooth (especially of tongue) First listed occurrence: Ezek 12 24.

definitions.full: H2509. chalaq חָלָק adjective smooth — 1 literal חָלָק אִישׁ Gen 27:11 (J), smooth man (opposed to שָׂעִר אישׁ ); הֶחָלָק הָהָר Josh 11:17 ; 12:7 the bald mountain (both D); southern limit of Josephus' conquest, identification dubious; (1) white cliffs 8 miles south of Dead Sea, and (2) Mt. Mâdara southwest from Pass es-‚afâ are proposed, see Di.; as substantive חַלְּקֵינַֿחַל Isa 57:6 (see I. חֵלֶק , 4 ) smooth (stones) of a brook-bed (ravine, wady), i.e. thou worshippest common round stones (contempt., see Che Di). 2 figurative of mouth uttering smooth words חִכָּהּ מִשֶּׁמֶן וְחָלָק Prov 5:3 ; compare 26:28 . 3 as substantive = flattery חָלָק מִקְסָם Ezek 12:24 divination of flattery .
